Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise proposal (PDF) and sample SCIM export with recommended mappings. High level below; full details are in the attached PDF and the CSV.

Summary (short):
- Roles: we support three canonical roles for Private Control Plane: control_plane_admin, control_plane_operator, control_plane_viewer.
- Identity types: SAML-authenticated users map to roles via SCIM group membership. Service accounts (for automation) are created as scoped service identities with a "service_account" role plus optional role bindings.
- Delegation: Customers can assign a subset of org admins as Delegated Admins — these are scoped to a VPC/tenant and can manage user/group role bindings but cannot alter billing or delete the tenant.
- Audit & retention: All role changes, service account creation, API key issuance, and SAML assertion events are emitted to audit logs that can be forwarded to customer SIEM. Default retention is 90 days; longer retention is configurable as an add-on.

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm the SAML metadata fields we expect from Acme (NameID format, group attribute path)? Dev, any constraints on service account key lifecycle we should call out? Stephanie — please add the compliance note re: SOC2 evidence for role changes.

Lauren Bishop

Thanks — adding a few technical specifics we require from the IdP:

- SAML metadata: we need a standard metadata XML (entityID, ACS URL, cert) — please send the file or authorize a metadata endpoint.
- Group attribute: prefer an array attribute named "groups" (multivalued). If your IdP nests attributes (e.g., enterprise apps path), indicate the full path.
- NameID: transient or persistent is fine; email as NameID is common and works for user mapping.

Example mapping (from attached CSV):
- SCIM group: "redwood-admins" => Redwood role: control_plane_admin
- SCIM group: "infra-operators" => Redwood role: control_plane_operator
- SCIM group: "read-only" => Redwood role: control_plane_viewer

Service accounts: our service accounts are minted with a short-lived key pair (default 7d), and rotating keys is supported via the API. If Acme needs longer lived keys, we recommend a vault-backed key with automated rotation.

I can take the SAML metadata and run a quick validation. Marcus
Senior Applied Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes from infra:

- Authorization model: we use a two-layer model — (1) role bindings at the tenant/VPC level, (2) resource-level grants for specific clusters or model endpoints. Delegated Admins get a scoped permission set (manage-users, manage-roles, view-logs) but cannot perform tenant-destructive actions.
- SCIM sync cadence: default 24h sync; we support near-real-time SCIM push but suggest event-driven SCIM webhooks for large orgs.
- Service account lifecycle: rotation_policy must be set; default: rotate keys every 7 days, max key lifetime 30d. We can add a mutual auth requirement for token minting endpoints for extra security.

Action for Acme: please confirm whether you want 24h SCIM or push-based. If push, we'll add webhook endpoints and a small firewall rule to allow Redwood's SCIM IPs.

Dev Patel
